title: Battle of Arginusae and the manning of the Athenian fleet with slaves
summary: In summer 406 BCE an Athenian fleet defeated a Spartan one off the Arginusae islands, between Lesbos and the Asian mainland. Xenophon says Athens manned 110 ships in thirty days by embarking all of military age, slave or free. A university lecture handout adds that a decree offered volunteering slaves freedom and citizenship, an unusual step not every Athenian welcomed; Athens lost 25 ships and Sparta 75.

uncertainty.note: Summer of 406 BCE per the Warwick handout; Xenophon notes are dated 406 B.C.

where.modern_name: Arginusae islands, off the Aegean coast of Turkey
where.historical_name: Arginusae (Arginousai) islands, opposite Mytilene between Lesbos and the Asia Minor mainland

importance.justification: A late Peloponnesian War sea battle whose manning policy offered slaves freedom and citizenship.

sources.title: Athenian politics, the war and Frogs (lecture handout, 2013)
sources.author: M. Griffith

reviewer_note: Least sure of the citizenship decree: only the Warwick handout states it on a page I opened (its text is OCR-garbled in places); Xenophon says only that slave or free were embarked. Pin is the island group.
